correctness.rationale: Full gradient list is computed from P. Its diagonal derivatives show singular support lies on a,b,c charts. For 2 invertible, elimination on a=1 gives exactly \(k[d,e]/(d^2e,de^2)\); its primary decomposition yields two smooth conic branches plus one embedded length-one point, symmetrically three such vertices, with Hilbert polynomial \(6m+3\). Hessian rank four verifies the generic transverse ordinary node. In characteristic two, exact elimination gives \(k[d,e,u]/(u^2)\), proving local ribbon structure. The globally defined three principal quadrics have height three, hence give an unmixed (2,2,2) complete intersection with Hilbert polynomial \(4m^2+2\). Its nilradical is locally invertible and globally \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)\); adjunction and H¹(P²,O(j))=0 establish K3 properties. The polynomial is primitive linear in a with coprime coefficients, and singular codimension≥2, so the cubic is integral and normal. The extracted script completed finite and exact polynomial checks. No finite count was used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Source-level distinction is substantive. The same symmetric permanent appears in Shafiei 2013, but only its apolar annihilator/rank is treated. The generic nonsymmetric permanent codimension considered by Alper–Bogart–Velasco is a different variety. Bangere et al. prove second-Veronese carpet nonexistence only over C, not positive characteristic. Comparisons of published mathematical records included exact characteristic-two symmetric determinant equivalence, conormal and odd-characteristic embedded points and found no decisive covered claim. This does not prove global uniqueness; a detailed older characteristic-two determinantal source might implicitly contain the result.

value.rationale: The object is the natural cubic hypersurface of symmetric 3-by-3 matrices, already studied through apolarity. Its intrinsic singular scheme changes unexpectedly from a three-conic arrangement with embedded length-one points in odd characteristic to a genus-five complete-intersection K3 carpet on the quadratic Veronese in characteristic two. The exact conormal \(\mathcal O(-3)\), square-zero local models, degree eight and canonical/cohomological invariants are structurally motivated, and the characteristic-two existence contrasts sharply with established complex nonexistence. This is substantive geometric information rather than a routine nonsmoothness criterion or unmotivated finite table.
